# Recovery Assertion

## H1 — Goal

Fix `run.sh` so it prints today’s four-digit year using a portable invocation that works with GNU and BSD `date`, then prints `done`. This is goal `y2p2-T3-shell-edge`, success criterion `SC-1`.

## H2 — Handoff Revision

The governing handoff is `handoff.md` at revision `b276f08f98bd968edbbf9f31db4d0a5fb12f1f11ed9700b1fe8a231761697914`, based on commit `5c07fdea1b3168ba3b4e6efb4bf12c359cbf5cfa`.

## H3 — Verified

No work is verified. The ledger contains only initialization and preparation of round `R-01`, slice `S1`; it contains no independent Conductor verification receipt.

## H4 — Unverified / In Progress

No ledger-backed progress exists. The slice target was observed as:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
date +%Y 2>/dev/null || date -j +%Y
echo not-done
```

This observation is unverified. Any uncommitted worktree content is observation only and must not be treated as progress, completion, or verification.

## H5 — Pending Action

The pending slice outcome is to update only `run.sh` so it uses one portable GNU/BSD-compatible invocation to print the four-digit year and then echoes `done`.

## H6 — Blockers

No task blocker is recorded. This recovery turn has no authority to perform the edit, execute task work, or declare completion. Shell execution and agent spawning are also denied for strict Phase 2 task execution.

## H7 — Legal Next Action

The next authorized task action is a single scoped edit to `run.sh`, using the slice-authorized Read/Edit/Write capabilities, replacing the non-portable/fallback behavior and `echo not-done` with the required portable year output followed by `echo done`. Afterward, the result remains only a candidate until independently gated, reviewed, and recorded by a distinct Conductor.

## H8 — Non-Goals / Forbidden Scope

There is no scope beyond the stated `run.sh` change. All other paths are outside slice `S1`. In particular, `.tad/scripts/`, `.claude/`, and `.tad/hooks/` are forbidden. Hidden acceptance artifacts must not be inspected.

## S1 — Why the Next Action Is Legal

Editing `run.sh` directly advances the declared `S1` outcome, maps to `SC-1`, stays within the sole allowed path, and uses only the capabilities listed in the current slice contract.

## S2 — Why Verified Work Must Not Be Redone

Governance prohibits redoing verified work because verification is authoritative ledger state. Here, the verified set is empty, so there is no verified implementation to repeat; the existing target content is merely an unverified observation.

## S3 — Why Blind Retry / Self-Completion Is Unavailable

There is no recorded failed attempt or verified checkpoint authorizing a retry. An executor cannot convert its own edit, prose, test result, or receipt into verified completion. Only a distinct Conductor may advance `verified` after the existing Gate and independent review both pass.

## S4 — What Is Rejected

Rejected actions include performing task work during this recovery assertion, editing anything except `run.sh`, touching forbidden paths, starting another slice, running unauthorized shell checks, spawning agents, inspecting hidden acceptance, treating observed or uncommitted content as completed work, redoing future verified work, issuing a blind retry, or declaring the goal complete without a bound independent Conductor verification receipt.
